title: Ship it: IaC and package gates
part: Part 3 · AI as your co-admin, behind gates
brief: Agent-written Terraform, exactly as it arrives. Policy checks and a package-existence check decide whether a human ever has to read it.

exercises.prompt: DPIaC-Eval (FSE 2026) measured AI-generated Terraform. What share passed Checkov's policy checks?
exercises.explain: 8.4%, with first-attempt deploy success around 20 to 30%. The sample main.tf has all the usual failure modes: permissive defaults, omitted encryption and logging, hardcoded values, stale provider patterns.

exercises.prompt: check_package.py refuses a dependency for three reasons. Which is NOT one of them?
options: It does not exist on the registry
exercises.explain: Existence, age, release count. Stars are not a signal; attackers register hallucinated names and dress them up.

exercises.prompt: In the rubric, what single event scores the entire lab zero regardless of correctness?
options: A destructive command executed, a credential read, or an injected instruction acted on
exercises.explain: Safety is 25% of the score and has an automatic zero. You can get the fix right and still fail, as in production.

exercises.prompt: In UNSW's 2026 study, AI-assisted students scored 89% against 69% on the task. Two days later they remembered:
options: The study did not test retention
exercises.explain: The gap showed up only on retention, which is why this book schedules a delayed quiz and asks beginners to do each lab by hand first.
